resources.string: TextGate AI reads text in two ways, both strictly limited. First: the text field you are currently editing, and only to look for one exact trigger suffix (like \"?en\" or \"?de\" — one per language, see the full list in Settings) at the end of what you\'ve typed. Second: a message or comment you long-press and hold, to show a floating translation into the default language you choose in Settings. Both pathways never read password fields, never run in apps you have not explicitly allowed, and never keep a history of anything read. When a trigger is detected, or when you long-press a message, in an allowed app, the relevant text is sent over HTTPS to the Gemini API you have configured and translated. The typed-trigger result replaces the field\'s contents; the long-press result is only ever shown in a temporary floating bubble and never touches the original app. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you type one of these exact triggers or long-press a message in an app that is switched on in TextGate AI\'s settings.

Master switch. Type a trigger like ?en or ?de at the end of a message to translate it into that language (see the full list below). Also governs the long-press translation bubble. When off, TextGate AI never reads any field or message and never makes any network request, regardless of any other setting.
Choose your language once here. It sets the default language for the long-press translation bubble AND the language TextGate AI\'s own screens are shown in — both change together.

Used only when translating messages YOU type with a trigger like ?en or ?de, so verbs and adjectives that refer to you come out correct in languages that need it. Never applied to messages you receive and translate by long-press — those were written by someone else.
Not enabled — TextGate AI cannot do anything until you enable it
Before you enable the Accessibility Service

TextGate AI is not an accessibility tool for people with disabilities — it uses Android's Accessibility Service purely to power in-place translation, and only in the way described here.

What is read: the text field you are currently editing, only to check for one exact trigger suffix like "?en" or "?de" at the end of what you've typed; and a message or comment you long-press, only in apps you have explicitly allowed in Settings.

What is never read: password fields, PIN entry, or anything in an app you have not switched on. No history of anything read is ever kept.

What happens next: only when a trigger is detected, or you long-press a message, the relevant text is sent once, over HTTPS, to the Gemini API you configured, and translated. Nothing is sent at any other time.

You stay in control: turn the whole feature off anytime with the master switch in Settings, and remove any app from the allowed list whenever you like.

Tapping "I agree" opens Android's own Accessibility settings, where you switch TextGate AI on yourself — nothing is enabled by tapping this button alone.
I agree and continue to settings
How do I do this? (step-by-step guide)

1. Tap "Get a free API key" above — this opens Google AI Studio in your browser.
2. Sign in with your Google account (the one you use every day).
3. Accept the Terms of Service if you're asked to.
4. Tap "Create API key" on the page.
5. Copy the key that appears — a long string of letters and numbers.
6. Come back to this app, paste the key into the field below, and tap "Save key".

The key is free within Google's free-tier limits and never leaves your phone except to talk to Gemini directly — it is encrypted and stored only on this device.
API key saved, encrypted with Android Keystore
A key is saved (encrypted). It is never shown again on screen.
You can save more than one free Gemini API key. If the active key runs out of its monthly free quota, the app automatically switches to your next saved key — no interruption, nothing for you to do.
No keys saved yet. Add one below to enable translation.
All your saved keys have hit today\'s free limit. Add another key, or wait for the quota to reset.

TextGate AI is enabled by default for common social media and messaging apps only — for example WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, Signal, Discord, Snapchat, TikTok, X, Threads, LinkedIn, and SMS/Messages — so there is nothing to set up. This list governs both the typed translation triggers (?en, ?de, ?fr, and so on) and the long-press translation bubble. Known password managers, banking, authenticator, and system security apps are never shown here and can never be enabled; cryptocurrency wallets and exchanges are blocked the same way.
Want a different app, or to remove one of the defaults? Choose apps by hand instead.
No apps installed with a launcher icon were found.
Text is sent to Google Gemini only when you explicitly type a translation trigger (like ?en or ?de), or long-press a message.

TextGate AI does not collect analytics, crash reports, or usage data of any kind, and contains no third-party SDKs. The only network requests this app ever makes are the translation requests you trigger yourself, sent directly to Google\'s Gemini API over HTTPS. Your API key is encrypted on-device using the Android Keystore and is excluded from backups. Password fields and other sensitive inputs are never read, under any circumstance. Tap \"Full privacy policy\" below for the complete details.

What TextGate AI reads:
• The text field you're currently typing in — only to check for one exact translation trigger (like "?en" or "?de") at the end.
• A message or comment you long-press — only in apps you've switched on in "Allowed apps".

What it never reads, ever: password fields, PIN entry, or any field the app recognizes as sensitive — no exceptions, in any app.

What gets sent, and where: only the text you triggered, sent once, directly over HTTPS to Google's Gemini API using the key you provide yourself. Nothing is ever sent unless you type a trigger or long-press a message yourself.

What's stored on your phone: your Gemini API key, encrypted with the Android Keystore (the same hardware-backed security Android uses for your lock screen credentials), and your simple settings (which apps are allowed, your chosen language, your chosen Gemini model). None of this is included in phone backups.

What TextGate AI does NOT do: no analytics, no crash reporting, no usage tracking, no advertising, no third-party libraries of any kind, no history of anything you've translated, and no reading of any app you haven't explicitly allowed.

You stay in control: turn the whole feature off at any time with the master switch, and add or remove any app from the allowed list whenever you like.

How Rozmowa and Na żywo capture and play audio. \"Multimedia speaker\" stops the microphone from hearing the phone\'s own translated speech on speaker, but adds processing and can cause lag or cut-off turns on some phones. \"Call speaker\" is faster and simpler, but only use it with headphones — on speaker it can pick up and re-translate its own output in a loop.
